senses.def: a flat board fixed to a wall or inside a cupboard, used for putting things on
examples: She put the vase on the top shelf, out of the kids' reach.
The new phone sold out within hours of hitting the shelves.

note: Plural: shelves. "Shelf life" = how long a product stays fresh or usable.

senses.def: the hard outer covering of an egg, nut, or animal such as a snail or crab
examples: Crack the eggs into a bowl and throw away the shells.
The kids spent the morning collecting shells on the beach.

senses.def: a metal case full of explosives that is fired from a large gun
examples: Shells landed near the hospital throughout the night.

note: "Come out of your shell" = become less shy and more confident.

senses.def: a place that protects you from bad weather or danger, or having a place to live
examples: Thousands of families are in urgent need of food and shelter.
We took shelter under a tree when the storm hit.

senses.def: to protect someone or something from weather or danger, or to stay somewhere for protection
examples: A tall hedge shelters the garden from the cold wind.
The hikers sheltered in a cave until the rain stopped.

note: "A sheltered life/childhood" = protected too much from the difficulties of the real world.

senses.def: a set period of work, especially when different groups of workers take turns
examples: She works the night shift at the hospital.
My shift starts at six, so I'll be home late.

senses.def: a change in position, direction, opinion, or policy
examples: Polls show a major shift in public opinion on the issue.

senses.def: to move something to a different place or position, or to change direction or focus
examples: Can you help me shift this sofa closer to the window?
The company has shifted its focus to online sales.

note: "Shift the blame (onto someone)" = make someone else seem responsible.

senses.def: to give out or reflect bright light
examples: The sun was shining when we left the house.
Her eyes were shining with excitement.

senses.def: to point a light in a particular direction
examples: He shined a flashlight into the dark basement.

senses.def: to be very good at something, so that people notice you
examples: She really shines in math and science.

note: Past form: shone /ʃoʊn/ (light) or shined (pointing a light, polishing shoes).

senses.def: smooth and bright, so that it reflects light
examples: He drove up in a shiny new sports car.
Wash your hair with this to make it soft and shiny.

senses.def: a large boat that carries people or goods across the sea
examples: The ship docked in the port early this morning.
There were over 3,000 passengers on board the cruise ship.

senses.def: to send goods to someone, by any kind of transport
examples: We ship all orders within two business days.
The company ships its products to over forty countries.

note: In American English, "ship" (verb) means to send by any method, including trucks and planes.

senses.def: ships considered as a group, or the business of carrying goods by ship
examples: The canal was closed to shipping for six days.
Rising fuel costs have hit the shipping industry hard.

senses.def: the act or cost of sending goods to customers
examples: Shipping is free on all orders over $50.

senses.def: a piece of clothing for the upper body, usually with a collar, sleeves, and buttons down the front
examples: He wore a white shirt and a tie to the interview.
Can you iron my blue shirt for tomorrow?

note: A "shirt" usually has a collar and buttons; Turkish "tişört" is a T-shirt.

senses.def: a strong feeling of surprise and upset, or the unpleasant event that causes it
examples: The news of his death came as a shock to everyone.
She was still in shock hours after the accident.

senses.def: to surprise and upset someone very much
examples: The violence in the film shocked many viewers.

senses.def: feeling or showing great surprise and upset
examples: I was shocked to hear that the store had closed.
There was a shocked silence when she announced her resignation.

note: Shocked = how you feel; shocking = what causes the feeling.

senses.def: very surprising and upsetting, or morally wrong
examples: The report revealed shocking levels of child poverty.
It's shocking that nobody was punished for the mistake.

senses.def: one of a pair of coverings for your feet, usually made of leather or plastic
examples: These shoes are comfortable enough to wear all day.
Please take off your shoes before you come in.

note: "In someone's shoes" = in their situation: "I wouldn't want to be in her shoes."

senses.def: to fire a gun or other weapon, or to hit someone with a bullet
examples: A police officer was shot in the leg during the chase.
Don't shoot! We're unarmed!

senses.def: to film or photograph something, or to kick or throw a ball toward the goal
examples: The movie was shot entirely in New Mexico.
He shoots with his left foot.

senses.def: a new part growing from a plant, or a session of taking photos or filming
examples: Green shoots appeared in the garden after the first warm week.
The model has a photo shoot in Miami tomorrow.

note: Irregular: shoot – shot – shot. "Green shoots" also means early signs of economic recovery.

senses.def: an event in which someone is shot with a gun
examples: Two people were injured in a shooting outside a nightclub.
Police are investigating the shooting.

senses.def: the process of filming a movie or TV show
examples: Shooting for the new series begins in March.

senses.def: a place where you can buy goods or services, or a place where things are made or repaired
examples: She runs a small coffee shop near the campus.
I took my car to the repair shop.

senses.def: to go to stores or websites to buy things
examples: We usually shop for groceries on Saturday mornings.
More people now shop online than in malls.

note: Americans usually say "store" for most places that sell things; "shop" is for small or specialist ones. "Shop around" = compare prices.

senses.def: the activity of buying things in stores or online
examples: I need to do some shopping before the guests arrive.
Online shopping has hurt many small retailers.

note: Say "go shopping" or "do the shopping", not "make shopping". US "shopping cart" = UK "trolley".

senses.def: the land along the edge of a sea, ocean, or lake
examples: We walked along the shore, collecting shells.
The boat was a mile from shore when the engine failed.

note: "Shore up" (phrasal verb) = support or strengthen something weak: "shore up the economy".

senses.def: small in length, distance, or time
examples: It's only a short walk from the hotel to the beach.
The meeting was short and to the point.

senses.def: smaller in height than most people
examples: He's a bit short for a basketball player.

senses.def: not having enough of something
examples: We're short of staff this week, so everyone is working extra hours.
I'm a little short on cash right now.

note: "Short for" = a shorter form of a name: "Liz is short for Elizabeth." "In short" = to summarize.

senses.def: lasting only a short time, or planned for the near future only
examples: The loan is only a short-term solution to the company's problems.
Lack of sleep can damage your short-term memory.

note: Opposite: long-term. Hyphenated before a noun, but no hyphen in "in the short term".

senses.def: a situation in which there is not enough of something that people need
examples: The hospital is facing a serious shortage of nurses.
Water shortages are common in the region during summer.

senses.def: soon, or a short time before or after something
examples: The doctor will see you shortly.
Shortly after midnight, the power went out.

note: "Shortly" means "soon", not "briefly" or "in a few words".

senses.def: the act of firing a gun, or the sound this makes
examples: Neighbors said they heard three shots around 2 a.m.

senses.def: a kick, throw, or hit toward a goal, or a photograph or a scene in a film
examples: Her shot from outside the box hit the post.
I got a great shot of the sunset.

senses.def: (informal, American) an injection of medicine
examples: Have you had your flu shot this year?

senses.def: (informal) an attempt to do something
examples: I've never tried surfing, but I'll give it a shot.

note: "A long shot" = something unlikely to succeed. "Big shot" (informal) = an important person.

senses.def: used to give advice or say what is right or sensible
examples: You should see a doctor about that cough.
Kids should wear helmets when they ride bikes.

senses.def: used to say that something is expected or probable
examples: The package should arrive by Friday.

senses.def: used with 'have' to say that something did not happen but would have been right
examples: You should have told me you were coming.

note: "Should have + past participle" criticizes or regrets past actions. Never "should to".

senses.def: either of the two parts of the body between the top of the arm and the neck
examples: She carried her bag over one shoulder.
He hurt his shoulder playing tennis.

note: As a verb, "shoulder the cost/blame/burden" = accept a difficult responsibility.

senses.def: to say something very loudly, often because you are angry or want to be heard
examples: Don't shout at me — I'm standing right here!
She shouted for help, but no one heard her.

senses.def: a loud cry of anger, fear, or excitement
examples: We heard shouts coming from the apartment upstairs.

note: "Shout at" someone = angrily; "shout to" someone = so they can hear you from far away.

senses.def: to let someone see something, or to explain how to do something
examples: Can you show me how this machine works?
She showed us photos of her trip.

senses.def: to make a fact or feeling clear, or to prove it
examples: The study shows that sleep improves memory.
He never shows his emotions.

senses.def: a program on TV or radio, or a performance or public event where things are displayed
examples: It's one of the most popular shows on TV right now.
They unveiled the new model at the car show.

note: Past participle: shown (sometimes showed). "Show up" = arrive, often late or unexpectedly.

senses.def: a device that sprays water on you to wash your body, or the act of washing this way
examples: I'm going to take a quick shower before dinner.
The shower in our hotel room didn't work.

senses.def: a short period of rain
examples: Scattered showers are expected this afternoon.

note: Americans "take a shower". A "baby shower" is a party with gifts for a woman expecting a baby.

senses.def: to become smaller, especially after being washed in hot water
examples: Wash it in cold water or it will shrink.
My favorite wool sweater shrinks a little every time I wash it.

senses.def: to become smaller in size, amount, or value
examples: The economy is expected to shrink by 2% this year.
The middle class has been shrinking for decades.

note: Irregular: shrink – shrank – shrunk. Informally, a "shrink" is a psychiatrist.

senses.def: to raise your shoulders and drop them to show you don't know or don't care
examples: When I asked where he'd been, he just shrugged.
She shrugged her shoulders and said, 'Who knows?'

senses.def: to treat something as unimportant or not worth worrying about
examples: The company shrugged off concerns about falling sales.

senses.def: to close something, or to become closed
examples: Please shut the door on your way out.
The factory was shut down after years of losses.

senses.def: not open
examples: Keep your eyes shut until I say so.

note: Irregular: shut – shut – shut. "Shut up" is rude; "Please be quiet" is polite.

senses.def: nervous and uncomfortable about meeting or talking to other people
examples: He was too shy to ask her to dance.
Don't be shy — come and say hello.

note: "Shy away from" = avoid something: "The company never shied away from risk."

senses.def: a brother or sister
examples: I have three siblings: two brothers and a sister.
Sibling rivalry is common in large families.

note: Fairly formal. In daily speech people say "brothers and sisters"; "sibling" is used when gender doesn't matter.

senses.def: physically or mentally ill
examples: She called in sick because she had a fever.
Half the class is out sick this week.

senses.def: feeling that you are going to vomit
examples: I felt sick after the long boat ride.

senses.def: bored or annoyed with something because it has happened too much
examples: I'm sick of hearing the same excuses.

note: In American English "sick" = ill in general. In British English "be sick" often means vomit.

senses.def: one of the two halves or edges of something, or a position to the left or right
examples: There's a gas station on the other side of the road.
She sleeps on her left side.

senses.def: one of the people or groups in an argument, war, or game
examples: She always takes her brother's side in an argument.

senses.def: a particular part or aspect of a situation or of someone's character
examples: City life has its good and bad sides.

note: "Look on the bright side" = focus on the positive part of a bad situation.

senses.def: to breathe out slowly and loudly to show you are tired, sad, or relieved
examples: She sighed and closed her laptop.
He sighs every time I mention the budget.

senses.def: the act or sound of breathing out slowly and loudly
examples: He let out a sigh of relief when the test results came back normal.

senses.def: the ability to see
examples: My grandfather is slowly losing his sight.

senses.def: the area that you can see from where you are
examples: The plane was soon out of sight.
There was no one in sight.

senses.def: something you see, especially something impressive, or famous places tourists visit
examples: The sunset over the canyon was an amazing sight.
We saw all the sights of Washington in two days.

note: Sight, site, and cite all sound the same (/saɪt/). "Love at first sight" = ilk görüşte aşk.

senses.def: something that shows that something exists, is happening, or may happen
examples: Losing weight without trying can be a sign of illness.
There's no sign of the rain stopping.

senses.def: a board or notice with words or pictures giving information or instructions
examples: The sign on the gate said 'No Parking'.

senses.def: to write your name on a document, or to make someone join a team by contract
examples: Please sign the form at the bottom.
The team signed a new striker last week.

note: "Sign up (for)" = register. Your written name is a "signature", not a "sign" (Turkish "imza").

senses.def: a movement, sound, or event that gives information, a warning, or an instruction
examples: The referee blew his whistle as a signal to stop play.
The rate cut sent a clear signal to investors.

senses.def: radio waves or electrical pulses that carry sounds or pictures
examples: I can't call you — there's no signal here.

senses.def: to make a movement or sound to give a message, or to show that something is likely
examples: The driver signaled before turning left.
The central bank signaled that rates would rise.

note: American spelling: signaled, signaling (British: signalled, signalling).

senses.def: your name written in your own special way, for example on a document
examples: The contract isn't valid without your signature.
Activists collected 10,000 signatures for the petition.

senses.def: a feature or style that makes someone or something easy to recognize
examples: Grilled octopus is the chef's signature dish.

senses.def: the importance or meaning of something, especially its effect on the future
examples: Few people understood the significance of the discovery at the time.
The date has special significance for our family.

senses.def: large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed
examples: There has been a significant increase in housing prices.
She played a significant role in the negotiations.

senses.def: in statistics, too large to be caused by chance
examples: The difference between the two groups was not statistically significant.

note: "Significant other" = your romantic partner (informal, American).

senses.def: by a large or important amount
examples: Prices have risen significantly over the past year.
The new drug significantly reduces the risk of a heart attack.

senses.def: used to show that a fact is important or meaningful
examples: Significantly, none of the managers attended the meeting.

senses.def: a complete lack of sound or of people speaking
examples: There was a long silence before anyone answered.
The crowd stood in silence to honor the victims.

senses.def: a refusal or failure to talk about something
examples: The government's silence on the issue has angered many voters.

senses.def: to make someone stop speaking or expressing their opinions
examples: The new law is an attempt to silence critics.

senses.def: with no sound, or making no sound
examples: The house was completely silent after the kids went to bed.
The 'k' in 'knife' is silent.

senses.def: not speaking, or not saying anything about a subject
examples: She remained silent throughout the police interview.

senses.def: a fine, soft, smooth cloth made from threads produced by silkworms
examples: She wore a red silk scarf to the party.
Silk was traded along routes connecting China to Europe.

senses.def: showing a lack of thought or good judgment, often in a harmless or funny way
examples: It was silly of me to leave my keys in the car.
The kids were making silly faces at the camera.

note: Milder and friendlier than "stupid"; often used playfully.

senses.def: a shiny, gray-white precious metal used for jewelry, coins, and decorative objects
examples: The necklace is made of solid silver.
My grandmother keeps the family silver in a locked cabinet.

senses.def: having a shiny, gray-white color
examples: He drives a silver pickup truck.
She won a silver medal in the 200 meters.

note: "Every cloud has a silver lining" = something good comes from every bad situation. US "silverware" = knives, forks, spoons.

senses.def: like someone or something else, but not exactly the same
examples: My sister and I have similar tastes in music.
The new model is similar to the old one but much lighter.

note: Use "similar to", not "similar with" (a common trap from Turkish "ile benzer").

senses.def: the fact of being alike, or a way in which two things are alike
examples: There are striking similarities between the two cases.
The similarity between the two brothers is remarkable.
